native.name: Native database replication
native.summary: The replication that ships inside PostgreSQL and MySQL, copying to another server of the same database.
native.bestWhen: you want a standby for failover or a read copy inside one database family.
native.watchOut: it copies between servers of the same database, and PostgreSQL logical replication does not copy schema changes.

goldengate.name: Oracle GoldenGate
goldengate.summary: An enterprise platform for one-way, two-way and multi-directional copies, strong on Oracle.
goldengate.bestWhen: you are an Oracle shop with the budget and may need two-way copies.
goldengate.watchOut: its FAQ lists Iceberg, but the write details are in separate GoldenGate DAA docs, and we do not quote an on-premises price.

dms.name: AWS DMS
dms.summary: AWS's managed service for one-time moves or ongoing replication, billed on instance or DCU hours.
dms.bestWhen: you are moving a database into AWS or doing simple replication inside AWS.
dms.watchOut: Iceberg is not a DMS target, there is no latency promise, and its two-way mode has no conflict resolution.

datastream.name: Google Cloud Datastream
datastream.summary: A serverless CDC service on Google Cloud, billed per GiB processed.
datastream.bestWhen: you are on Google Cloud and land data in BigQuery.
datastream.watchOut: there is no self-hosted option, and Iceberg streaming is append-only, so no updates and deletes.

debezium.name: Debezium
debezium.summary: An open-source, Apache 2.0 CDC engine that you run yourself; this guide covers Debezium Server.
debezium.bestWhen: you already run Kafka or are happy to run the pieces yourself.
debezium.watchOut: you run all of it, and the Iceberg sink is community-maintained in a separate repository.

olake.name: OLake Go
olake.summary: An open-source tool for log-based CDC from PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, MongoDB and SQL Server into Iceberg or Parquet.
olake.bestWhen: you run one of those databases and want Iceberg tables on storage you control.
olake.watchOut: output is Apache Iceberg or Parquet on storage you choose.

estuary.name: Estuary
estuary.summary: A managed platform for streaming and batch, billed at $0.50 per GB plus connector fees.
estuary.bestWhen: you want one managed platform that does streaming and batch.
estuary.watchOut: every source and destination is billed, and its Iceberg connector needs an AWS EMR Serverless Spark application.

airbyte.name: Airbyte
airbyte.summary: A long connector list with a free self-hosted Core edition and a Cloud plan from $20 a month.
airbyte.bestWhen: a delay of minutes to an hour is fine and you want many connectors.
airbyte.watchOut: it syncs on a schedule, not as a live stream, and its CDC does not pick up TRUNCATE or table-structure changes.
